To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bounded-operator style is a natural and convenient approach to the verification of real-time systems, and that it is possible to verify bounded-invariance properties and bounded-response properties in a compositional manner.
(a) the bounded-operator style allows us to verify real-time properties in an intuitive way and that (b) the explicit-clock style provides an efficient alternative to the bounded-operator style.

(i) the verification of real-time properties is a conservative extension of the verification of non-time-critical properties and (ii) the verification of explicit-clock specifications is a conservative extension (in the sense of the second item above) of the verification of bounded specifications.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a generalization of temporal logic and the corresponding verification framework that can be used to verify real-time properties of real-time systems in the context of the underlying computational model.
the development of a comprehensive and systematic approach to the specification and verification of real-time systems.
a formalism for the specification and verification of real-time systems, and with two complementary proof methodologies for establishing real-time properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the explicit clock approach is the preferred one for real-time system verification.

we provide an adequate framework for the specification and verification of real-time properties of systems with shared variables and/or message passing communication, and that the two proof methods presented are adequate for the verification of bounded-response properties and time-bounded safety properties, respectively, of such systems.
the explicit-clock style is the most natural and the easiest to handle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general theory for real-time system verification that is both sound and complete and that is applicable to a broad class of real-time systems.
the explicit-clock style is more general than the bounded-operators style and the proof methodology of bounded-invariance is more efficient than the proof methodology of safety properties.
we have developed a framework for specifying and verifying real-time systems that can be viewed as a conservative extension of the traditional temporal logic approach to reactive systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the verification of real-time properties, we do not need to develop new proof rules or new proof methods.
the explicit-clock style is a much simpler approach for verifying time-bounded properties.

the verification of real-time properties of timed transition system can be done in a modular way, i.e., by verifying the properties of individual modules separately, and by composing the modules in such a way that the composition preserves the timing properties.
